title: Grateful Dead Live at War Memorial on 1973-03-31
lineage: Reel master > cassette > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy second set with scorching 'He's Gone', a surprise 'I Know You Rider' out of space, and Jerry's relentless riffs.
ai_review.review: The recording sounds clear – the mix lets Keith’s keys shine and captures the band’s dynamics without noticeable flaws. Musically the show is a roller‑coaster: a mellow first set that builds into a blistering second half highlighted by 'He's Gone', an inventive 'Other One' segue into 'I Know You Rider', and a fiery 'Sugar Magnolia'.

ai_rating.rationale: One detailed, five‑star review praises both performance and sound quality; the show is described as outstanding and the recording as clear, leading to a high combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: No complaints about drop‑outs or muddiness; reviewer notes "Keith nice in the mix" indicating a clean, balanced board recording.

standout_songs: The Other One (I Know You Rider out of Space)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set described as mellow and relaxed, second set jumps in with high energy, strong transitions (Promised > Bertha > Greatest) and an unexpected rider out of space that elevates the performance.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Riffs hard throughout, especially on El Paso and 'He's Gone'; never stops delivering licks.
band_member_comments.Phil: Good bass riffs and solid baritone backing vocals noted.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's keyboards are praised as "nice in the mix".
band_member_comments.Drums: Billy hits the skins for a brief 1:33‑second burst; otherwise no specific drum commentary.
